gloss: mailing (a letter); posting (in a mailbox); dropping into a box

definitions.gloss: the act of mailing a letter or postcard by dropping it into a public mailbox or post-office collection box; the act of dropping a slip into a designated collection box (e.g. a comment box, raffle box, or election ballot box)
definitions.explanation: The standard formal word for the action of putting a letter, postcard, application form, or similar item into a collection box. Most often used about postal mail dropped into a {郵便|ゆうびん}ポスト (street mailbox), but it also covers ballot voting, prize-draw entries, and any context in which something is dropped into a labelled box. Used as a noun and as a する-verb ({投函|とうかん}する 'to mail, to post').

examples.japanese: {手紙|てがみ}を{投函|とうかん}した。
{駅前|えきまえ}のポストに{葉書|はがき}を{投函|とうかん}してきた。
examples.english: I just dropped a postcard in the mailbox in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {応募|おうぼ}{用紙|ようし}は{切手|きって}を{貼|は}って、{締|し}め{切|き}り{日|び}までに{投函|とうかん}してください。
examples.english: Please put a stamp on the application form and mail it by the deadline.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{中|なか}を{近|ちか}くのポストまで{歩|ある}いて、{大切|たいせつ}な{書類|しょるい}を{投函|とうかん}した。
examples.english: I walked to the nearby mailbox in the rain and mailed an important document.

notes:
Composed of {投|とう} ('to throw') + {函|かん} ('box'). The character {函|かん} is the same as {箱|はこ} ('box') and is the formal Sino-Japanese reading. Literally 'to throw into a box'.

USAGE:
{投函|とうかん} is the standard, slightly formal word used in postal contexts and on instructions for mail and applications. It is the word the Japanese postal service ({日本|にっぽん}{郵便|ゆうびん}) uses on its signs and notices, and it is what application forms instruct you to do. In casual speech, Japanese speakers often instead say ポストに{入|い}れる ('to put in the mailbox') or {手紙|てがみ}を{出|だ}す ('to send a letter').

Used both as a plain noun and as a する-verb: {投函|とうかん}する 'to mail, to post (something)'.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Transitive in its する-verb form. The thing being mailed is marked with を, and the location with に:
- {手紙|てがみ}をポストに{投函|とうかん}する: to drop a letter in the mailbox
- The passive {投函|とうかん}される is also common in postal-service notices.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手紙|てがみ}を{投函|とうかん}する: to mail a letter
- {葉書|はがき}を{投函|とうかん}する: to mail a postcard
- ポストに{投函|とうかん}する: to drop into a mailbox
- {投票|とうひょう}{用紙|ようし}を{投函|とうかん}する: to drop a ballot into the ballot box
- {投函|とうかん}{日|び}: posting date, mailing date
- {投函|とうかん}{時|じ}: at the time of mailing
- {投函口|とうかんぐち}: mail slot, drop-off slot (the opening of the box)
- {投函|とうかん}{完了|かんりょう}: 'mailed' (a status notification)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手紙|てがみ}を{出|だ}す: to send a letter — the everyday spoken expression; covers both the act of mailing and the broader act of writing and sending. More casual.
- ポストに{入|い}れる: to put in the mailbox — a plain spoken paraphrase of {投函|とうかん}する.
- {郵送|ゆうそう}: mailing, sending by post — refers to the broader act of sending something through the postal system, including parcels handed over at a post office counter.
- {発送|はっそう}: dispatch, sending out — more general; commonly used by online retailers about shipping orders.
- {差|さ}し{出|だ}す: to send (a letter); to submit — formal verb for handing over or submitting documents.

REGISTER:
Formal/written. Common in postal-service signage, instructions on application forms, and news articles. In conversation, native speakers usually prefer the more colloquial {出|だ}す or ポストに{入|い}れる.
